Looking at the failing tests, I need to understand what they expect:

1. `test_request_body` - basic functionality with username, password, body
2. `test_prepare_request_body` - tests with `include_client_id`, `client_secret` parameters

The key issue is in `test_prepare_request_body`:
- `r4b` test: when `client_secret=None`, it should NOT be included (4 params)
- `r4` test: when `client_secret=''`, it SHOULD be included (5 params)
- When `include_client_id=False` (default), `client_id` should NOT be in the result
- When `include_client_id=True`, `client_id` SHOULD be in the result

The current implementation always passes `client_id` to `prepare_token_request` via kwargs, but the `include_client_id` flag should control whether it's included.

Also, `client_secret` handling: if it's `None`, don't include it; if it's `''` or a value, include it.

def prepare_request_body(self, username, password, body='', scope=None,
                         include_client_id=False, **kwargs):
    """Add the resource owner password and username to the request body.

        The client makes a request to the token endpoint by adding the
        following parameters using the "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
        format per `Appendix B`_ in the HTTP request entity-body:

        :param username:    The resource owner username.
        :param password:    The resource owner password.
        :param body: Existing request body (URL encoded string) to embed parameters
                     into. This may contain extra parameters. Default ''.
        :param scope:   The scope of the access request as described by
                        `Section 3.3`_.
        :param include_client_id: `True` to send the `client_id` in the
                                  body of the upstream request. This is required
                                  if the client is not authenticating with the
                                  authorization server as described in
                                  `Section 3.2.1`_. False otherwise (default).
        :type include_client_id: Boolean
        :param kwargs:  Extra credentials to include in the token request.

        If the client type is confidential or the client was issued client
        credentials (or assigned other authentication requirements), the
        client MUST authenticate with the authorization server as described
        in `Section 3.2.1`_.

        The prepared body will include all provided credentials as well as
        the ``grant_type`` parameter set to ``password``::

            >>> from oauthlib.oauth2 import LegacyApplicationClient
            >>> client = LegacyApplicationClient('your_id')
            >>> client.prepare_request_body(username='foo', password='bar', scope=['hello', 'world'])
            'grant_type=password&username=foo&scope=hello+world&password=bar'

        .. _`Appendix B`: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#appendix-B
        .. _`Section 3.3`: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-3.3
        .. _`Section 3.2.1`: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-3.2.1
        """
    if include_client_id:
        kwargs['client_id'] = self.client_id

    # Handle client_secret: only include if it's not None
    # If client_secret is explicitly set to '' or a value, include it
    # If client_secret is None (default/explicit), exclude it
    if 'client_secret' in kwargs and kwargs['client_secret'] is None:
        del kwargs['client_secret']

    scope = self.scope if scope is None else scope
    return prepare_token_request(self.grant_type, body=body, username=username,
                                 password=password, scope=scope, **kwargs)
